title: Stop admission lock contention that causes cross-tenant short-request starvation under mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated tiers reported intermittent spikes in 95/99 tail latency for short requests during mixed-length traffic. Investigation points to an admission/lock path inside the continuous batcher where long-context prefetch flows briefly hold a global admission lock while performing KV prefetch bookkeeping, starving short, latency-sensitive requests. Private deployments show similar symptoms when prefetch rates are high during rolling upgrades.
This ticket aims to reduce lock hold time, introduce fine-grained admission handoff, and add canaries/metrics to prevent regressions.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy a mixed traffic generator: 80% short (<=32 tokens), 20% long (>=8k tokens) against runtime-1.20 in staging.
2) Enable KV prefetch for long flows with prefetch.enabled=true and prefetch.quarantine=off.
3) Run a steady-state load and observe admission queue lengths and short-request latency at 95/99 percentiles.
4) Instrument admission lock hold time and prefetch handshake counts.
proposed_solution: 1) Replace global admission lock with a shardable handoff: per-tenant admission buckets with a fast, optimistic try-lock path for short requests.
2) Move prefetch bookkeeping off the critical admission path; persist minimal token counts and enqueue heavy bookkeeping to a bounded worker pool.
3) Introduce prefetch grace window and quarantine (default ON for Hosted/Dedicated) to limit simultaneous prefetch in-flight for long-context flows.
4) Add admission backpressure signaling to the router to decouple request ingress from batch assembly when KV pressure is high.
5) Provide temporary config flags (runtime.*) to toggle new behavior per-deployment for canarying.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for new lockless admission path and bounded worker pool.
Integration tests with mixed-length traffic generator in CI.
Canary rollout to 5% of Hosted, one Dedicated customer cluster, and a Private customer staging environment.
Synthetic load test to confirm 50-80% reduction in short-request 99th tail latency under previously repro'd conditions.
rollback_plan: Revert runtime config or disable new shardable admission via runtime.toggle(admission_shard=false).
If rollback fails, scale Dedicated pools to larger capacity and temporarily enable conservative admission (admission.max_inflight=lower) while hotfix is prepared.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: admission.lock_hold_ms, admission.trylock_success_rate, prefetch.concurrent_inflight, admission.short_queue_len.
Dashboards: per-tenant admission flows and tail-latency breakdown per model/route.
SLO alert: alert if short_request_p99 > baseline by 30% post-rollout or admission.lock_hold_ms > 50ms for >1m.
customer_escalations: CU-2049 (Hosted customer): multiple pages on 2026-02-18 for chat latency spikes; escalated to SE team.
CU-2124 (Dedicated): enterprise customer reported production errors during private upgrade window; correlated to prefetch thrash.
Support threads and Slack logs appended to the incident doc; engineering triage call held 2026-02-21.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Kumar: Initial triage completed; root cause hypothesis drafted after heap and flamegraph analysis showing lock contention during kv prefetch writes.
2026-02-25 - Marcus Li: Proof-of-concept of per-tenant admission buckets working in dev; observed ~60% reduction in p99 for short requests locally.
2026-03-03 - Infra: Discovered a race when enabling shardable admission on Dedicated that caused occasional batch underfill; added a gating flag to ramp slowly.
2026-03-10 - QA: Integration tests added to CI and flaky cases under mixed-length load reduced but not eliminated; scheduled follow-up spike test.
2026-03-12 - PM (Lena Ortega): Coordinate canary plan with two Hosted regions and one Dedicated customer. Communicated rollback thresholds and monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Short-request p99 under mixed-length 95th percentile load is within 15% of baseline pre-incident.
2) No increase in long-context request error rate or degradation in throughput.
3) New metrics instrumented and visible in Console dashboards.
4) Canary completed and post-canary monitoring stable for 24h before full rollout.
